intro: Here on the coast lies Heraclea Pontica, an ancient city in Zonguldak province with a history running from 560 BC to the 4th century AD. It was a Bithynian coastal city founded by Megarians, and it is the setting of the legend of Heracles.
history: Around 560 BC, colonists from Megara founded the city, and it grew into a powerful city-state in the rich Black Sea trade. But Heraclea was famous for more than trade. The Greeks believed that Heracles descended to the underworld through the Cehennemağzı caves here.
structure-1: You are now at the Cehennemağzı Caves, the sacred caves where Herakles was said to have captured Cerberus. Pause at the entrance and let the legend come alive.
structure-2: Here are the remains of the Sanctuary of Heracles, a sacred precinct dedicated to Herakles, the hero at the heart of this city's story.
structure-3: Now look at the City Walls. These defensive walls encircled the city, and they were rebuilt over the centuries.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Harbour and the Necropolis.
facts: Did you know? Clearchus, one of antiquity's philosopher-tyrants, seized power here, and the city was known for its philosophical school. Antiquity held that the caves here, Cehennemağzı, the Mouth of Hell, were where Heracles dragged Cerberus up from the underworld. And as a Megarian colony, the city is singled out in ancient sources for reducing the native Mariandynians to serfdom.
outro: This brings our tour of Heraclea Pontica to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
